answer: Assign each agent one distinct 10 GB chunk from a shared atlas, and pull a random piece of it for checking every week. A sparrow sized identity still has to keep the whole chunk online, because the audit asks for bytes from an unpredictable offset, and a stored hash or link fails that test. Agents that pass keep working, agents that fail lose the slot, so a farm has to pay for real disks. Faking 1,000 identities means 10 TB of storage, about $230 each month at $0.023 per GB, plus the traffic for weekly checks, and a velvet cover story does not change the bill.
